cases.drop_reason: The record is a bank designated for moving a cocaine network's proceeds; it shows no one placed inside the bank or controlling it.

cases.n: Banco Delta Asia
cases.d: Designated by FinCEN over accounts held for North Korean entities, including proceeds described as coming from narcotics and counterfeit currency. The action froze roughly $25 million and cut the bank out of dollar clearing; it is the clearest demonstration that a designation reaches further than a prosecution.
cases.cite: FinCEN Section 311 finding, September 2005; final rule 2007
cases.rank: Small bank — sovereign client accounts (banks & money transmission), Macau
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: FBME Bank
cases.d: Registered in Tanzania and operated from Cyprus, it was named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern over accounts used by organised crime and sanctioned parties. Cyprus resolved the bank; the owners' arbitration against the designation ran for years afterwards.
cases.cite: FinCEN Section 311 notice, July 2014; final rule 2016
cases.rank: Offshore bank — non-resident shell accounts (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: U.S. Bancorp
cases.d: Deferred prosecution and $613 million in penalties after admitting it capped the number of alerts its monitoring software could generate so that the workload matched the size of its compliance staff. The bank also failed to report a customer running an unlicensed payday lending business.
cases.cite: US v. U.S. Bank National Association, S.D.N.Y., DPA February 2018
cases.rank: Retail bank — transaction monitoring (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: Capital One
cases.d: Fined $390 million by FinCEN over its Check Cashing Group unit, which processed roughly $16 billion for clients including businesses whose organised-crime associations the bank's own files had recorded. The relationships continued for years after the warnings.
cases.cite: FinCEN consent order, January 2021
cases.rank: Correspondent banking — check-cashing clients (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: MoneyGram International
cases.d: A 2012 deferred prosecution and $100 million forfeiture over agents processing fraud and structured transfers was followed in 2018 by a further $125 million when the company was found to have breached the agreement's terms. The agent model puts the compliance duty on thousands of small franchises and the penalty on the brand.
cases.cite: US v. MoneyGram International Inc., M.D. Pa., DPA November 2012; amended settlement November 2018
cases.rank: Money transmission — agent network (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: Deutsche Bank
cases.d: Fined about $630 million by US and UK regulators over mirror trades that moved roughly $10 billion out of Russia through its Moscow, London and New York desks, and a further $150 million by New York in 2020 for onboarding failures. Laundering infrastructure rather than a drug case: the same channel carries any proceeds that need distance from their origin.
cases.cite: NYDFS and FCA consent orders, January 2017; NYDFS consent order, July 2020
cases.rank: Correspondent banking — mirror trades (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: Swedbank
cases.d: Fined 4 billion kronor by the Swedish regulator over high-risk non-resident flows through its Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian branches and misleading disclosures about them. The Baltic corridor's laundering capacity outlived the Danske case by several years.
cases.cite: Finansinspektionen decision, March 2020
cases.rank: Baltic branch network — non-resident flows (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: ABN AMRO
cases.d: Settled with Dutch prosecutors for €480 million after admitting years of failures in customer checks and reporting. Three former executives were separately named as suspects, which is rare: in most cases at this scale the institution pays and no individual is charged.
cases.cite: Openbaar Ministerie settlement, April 2021
cases.rank: Universal bank — client due diligence (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record is a financial institution designated or penalised for weak monitoring; it shows no crime group placing or paying staff inside it or controlling it.

cases.n: Silk Road
cases.d: The first large anonymous drug marketplace, handling several hundred million dollars in sales before its seizure in 2013. Its operator was convicted on seven counts and sentenced to life without parole in 2015; he was pardoned in January 2025 and released.
cases.cite: US v. Ulbricht, S.D.N.Y., verdict February 2015, sentence May 2015; presidential pardon January 2025
cases.undone: Operator pardoned by the US president in January 2025 and released from a life sentence.
cases.drop_reason: A darknet market run by its own operator; no outside party got inside an institution.

cases.n: AlphaBay
cases.d: Ten times the size of Silk Road at its peak and seized in a joint operation in July 2017. Its administrator was arrested in Bangkok and died in custody a week later, which ended the prosecution before any of the evidence was tested.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice and Europol operation, July 2017; S.D. Fla. indictment
cases.drop_reason: A darknet market and its administrator's own crimes, with no outside party inside a government or company.

cases.n: Hansa Market
cases.d: Dutch police took over the market's servers and ran it themselves for 27 days, collecting addresses and passwords from users fleeing the AlphaBay seizure. The tactic reversed the usual sequence: the takedown came after the surveillance rather than instead of it.
cases.cite: Dutch National Police and Europol, Operation Bayonet, July 2017
cases.rank: Darknet marketplace — covert operation (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: Police taking over and running a criminal marketplace is a police operation, not infiltration.

cases.n: Wall Street Market
cases.d: Three German administrators were arrested in 2019 after attempting to abscond with roughly €11 million held in escrow. They were convicted in Germany; a US indictment named them and two prolific vendors.
cases.cite: Landgericht Kleve proceedings, verdicts 2021; C.D. Cal. indictment, May 2019
cases.drop_reason: Market administrators stealing escrow funds is their own crime, with no outside party inside an institution.

cases.n: Helix
cases.d: A mixing service that laundered roughly 350,000 bitcoin, much of it from darknet drug markets it partnered with directly. Its operator pleaded guilty to a laundering conspiracy and was fined $60 million by FinCEN — the first such penalty against a mixer.
cases.cite: US v. Harmon, D.D.C., plea August 2021; FinCEN civil penalty, October 2020
cases.drop_reason: A mixing service laundering for darknet markets is a criminal service openly selling to criminals, not infiltration.

cases.n: Bitcoin Fog
cases.d: The longest-running mixing service, moving about 1.2 million bitcoin over a decade, a large share of it darknet drug proceeds. Its operator was convicted at trial in March 2024 on blockchain analysis that reached back to transactions made in 2011.
cases.cite: US v. Sterlingov, D.D.C., verdict March 2024, sentence November 2024
cases.drop_reason: A laundering service run by its own operator; no one got inside a government or company.

cases.n: Bitzlato
cases.d: Named by FinCEN as a primary money-laundering concern in the first use of a new sanctions authority. Officials described over $700 million in transfers with Hydra alone between 2018 and 2022, in both directions: buyers funded purchases from Bitzlato accounts and vendors sent the takings back to them.
cases.cite: FinCEN order under Section 9714(a), January 2023; US v. Legkodymov, E.D.N.Y.
cases.rank: Exchange — deposits from darknet markets (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: A crypto exchange named a money-laundering concern for processing darknet payments is weak or criminal compliance, not infiltration.

cases.n: Garantex
cases.d: Sanctioned by OFAC in April 2022 for processing proceeds from Hydra and ransomware operators. Estonia had already withdrawn its licence; the exchange kept operating from Moscow, which is the practical limit of designating an entity inside a jurisdiction that will not act on it.
cases.cite: OFAC designation, April 2022; Estonian FIU licence revocation, February 2022
cases.drop_reason: An exchange sanctioned for processing illicit proceeds is a designation, with no outside party placed inside it.

cases.n: ChipMixer
cases.d: German and US authorities seized the service's servers and about €44 million in bitcoin, citing roughly $700 million in laundered funds from darknet markets and ransomware. It broke deposits into uniform chips so that no output amount could be matched to an input.
cases.cite: BKA and US Department of Justice seizure, March 2023
cases.drop_reason: A mixing service seized for laundering is its own crime, not infiltration.

cases.n: Incognito Market
cases.d: A market that sold prescription pills, many of them counterfeit and fentanyl-laced, and closed by extorting its own users with the threat of publishing their transaction records. Its operator was arrested at JFK in May 2024 and charged in Manhattan.
cases.cite: US v. Rui-Siang Lin, S.D.N.Y., complaint May 2024
cases.drop_reason: A darknet market extorting its users is its own operator's crime, not infiltration.

cases.n: Port of Hamburg — terminal access
cases.d: Sixteen tonnes of cocaine hidden in tins of putty were found in a single Hamburg container in February 2021, the largest seizure in Europe at the time. German prosecutions have reached dock workers and hauliers; volumes rose here as Antwerp and Rotterdam hardened, which is displacement rather than growth.
cases.cite: German customs (Zoll) seizure announcement, February 2021; Hamburg court proceedings
cases.rank: Container terminals — dock and clearance staff (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: The record describes a cocaine seizure and prosecutions; it does not show smugglers placing or paying insiders at the port.

cases.n: The Zheng fentanyl network
cases.d: A father and son were indicted in Ohio and designated by OFAC as a fentanyl trafficking organisation that manufactured analogues to order and shipped them by post to buyers in at least 25 countries. Both remain in China; the case established the pattern the later precursor indictments follow.
cases.cite: US v. Fujing Zheng and Guanghua Zheng, N.D. Ohio, indictment 2018; OFAC designation August 2019
cases.rank: Chemical manufacture and mail-order export (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: A trafficking family making and posting fentanyl is smuggling, with no one inside an institution.

cases.n: Indian opioid exports to West Africa
cases.d: An investigation traced tapentadol and carisoprodol combinations, unapproved for sale in either the exporting or the importing country, from Indian manufacturers to street markets in Ghana, Nigeria and Cote d'Ivoire. India's drug regulator suspended export permissions and inspected the plants named; the companies deny wrongdoing.
cases.cite: BBC Eye investigation, February 2025; CDSCO enforcement action, 2025
cases.drop_reason: Manufacturers exporting unapproved opioids is a sales and regulation issue, not infiltration.

cases.n: Insys Therapeutics
cases.d: The founder and four executives were convicted of racketeering for bribing prescribers to write a fentanyl spray licensed only for cancer breakthrough pain, and running a unit that lied to insurers to get the prescriptions covered. The founder was sentenced to 66 months; the company filed for bankruptcy days after pleading guilty.
cases.cite: US v. Kapoor et al., D. Mass., verdict May 2019, sentence January 2020
cases.rank: Manufacturer — sales force and prior authorisation (pharmaceutical supply)
cases.drop_reason: Company executives bribing private prescribers is the company's own fraud; no outside party got inside a government or company.

cases.n: Walmart, CVS and Walgreens
cases.d: The three chains agreed to pay about $13.8 billion over 15 years to settle claims that their pharmacies filled opioid prescriptions their own systems had flagged. A federal jury had already found the three liable for creating a public nuisance in two Ohio counties.
cases.cite: National Prescription Opiate Litigation, N.D. Ohio, settlements November 2022; Lake and Trumbull County verdict, November 2021
cases.drop_reason: Pharmacies settling claims over filling flagged prescriptions is their own failure, not infiltration.

cases.n: Mallinckrodt
cases.d: The largest US manufacturer of generic oxycodone agreed to $1.7 billion in opioid settlement payments through its bankruptcy, having earlier paid $35 million to resolve DEA findings that it failed to report suspicious orders. Its output at one point exceeded the rest of the generic market combined.
cases.cite: In re Mallinckrodt plc, D. Del., plan confirmed 2022; DEA administrative settlement 2017
cases.drop_reason: A manufacturer's settlement over suspicious orders is its own conduct, not infiltration.

cases.n: Teva and Allergan
cases.d: Teva agreed to about $4.25 billion in cash and generic naloxone supply to settle US opioid claims, and Allergan to $2.37 billion. Neither admitted wrongdoing, and the naloxone component means part of the settlement is paid in the antidote to the product.
cases.cite: National opioid settlements announced November and July 2022
cases.drop_reason: Opioid settlements by manufacturers concern their own conduct, not an outside party inside them.

cases.n: Indivior
cases.d: Resolved US charges for $600 million after a subsidiary pleaded guilty to a felony over marketing an opioid dependence film as safer around children than it had evidence to claim. Its former parent paid $1.4 billion separately, and its former chief executive pleaded guilty to a misdemeanour.
cases.cite: US v. Indivior Solutions, W.D. Va., plea July 2020; Reckitt Benckiser resolution 2019
cases.drop_reason: Misleading drug marketing by a company is its own offence, not infiltration.

cases.n: The Star Entertainment Group
cases.d: A NSW inquiry found the company unsuitable to hold its Sydney licence after evidence it disguised gambling spend as hotel expenses on China UnionPay cards and extended large credit lines to patrons whose organised-crime links had been reported internally. AUSTRAC took it to the Federal Court over 117 high-risk patrons and its dealings with the Suncity junket operator, and sought a penalty of A$400 million. The company argued a penalty that size would render it insolvent, and it was rescued by a A$300 million investment. Two former senior executives admitted breaches and were penalised; the Federal Court found two more had breached their duties in 2026.
cases.cite: Bell Review report, NSW Independent Liquor and Gaming Authority, September 2022; AUSTRAC Federal Court proceedings and penalty hearing, June 2025; ASIC proceedings against former executives, 2025-2026
cases.rank: Casino operator — junkets and credit (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: The record shows a casino failing anti-money-laundering duties and serving risky patrons, not a crime group placing staff in or controlling it.

cases.n: Tak Chun Group
cases.d: Macau's second-largest junket operator ran under-the-table betting alongside the licensed tables, on a scale prosecutors put in the billions. Its chairman was sentenced to 14 years in April 2023 for criminal association, illegal gambling and aggravated laundering; the fraud counts were overturned on appeal.
cases.cite: Court of First Instance, Macau SAR, April 2023; Court of Second Instance, January 2024
cases.drop_reason: A junket operator running illegal side betting is its own crime, not infiltration.

cases.n: MGM Grand and The Cosmopolitan
cases.d: Both properties entered non-prosecution agreements and forfeited $7.45 million over years of taking play from an illegal bookmaker whose income they had reason to question. A former MGM Grand president was separately convicted of failing to file the required report.
cases.cite: US Attorney, C.D. Cal., non-prosecution agreements January 2024; US v. Sibella, conviction 2024
cases.rank: Casinos — host and compliance staff (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: Casinos taking play from an illegal bookmaker is failed monitoring, not infiltration.

cases.n: British Columbia casinos — the Cullen Commission
cases.d: A public inquiry found that hockey bags of $20 notes were accepted at Lower Mainland casinos for years while regulators and government knew and did not act. The commissioner declined to call it wilful blindness by individuals and located the failure in the institutions instead.
cases.cite: Commission of Inquiry into Money Laundering in British Columbia, final report, June 2022
cases.rank: Casino operators and the provincial regulator (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: The inquiry located the failure in casinos and regulators ignoring cash, and declined to find individuals complicit; no outside party was shown inside.

cases.n: Aleman, Cordero, Galindo & Lee (Alcogal)
cases.d: The firm that replaced Mossack Fonseca as the region's largest incorporator appeared throughout the Pandora Papers, having formed thousands of structures whose beneficial owners it had not verified. It says it complied with the law in force at the time; no charge has been brought.
cases.cite: ICIJ Pandora Papers, October 2021
cases.rank: Offshore formation agent (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A firm forming companies without verifying owners is a compliance failure; no charge and no outside party inside it.

cases.n: US anonymous company formation
cases.d: Delaware, Wyoming and Nevada companies can be formed in minutes with no verified owner, and appear repeatedly in trafficking and laundering files. The Corporate Transparency Act was to end that from 2024; an interim rule in March 2025 exempted domestic companies from reporting, leaving the requirement on foreign entities only.
cases.cite: Corporate Transparency Act 2021; FinCEN interim final rule, March 2025
cases.rank: Corporate registry as a service (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A gap in US company-formation law is a regulatory issue, not infiltration.

cases.n: ANOM — Operation Trojan Shield
cases.d: After Phantom Secure closed, the FBI and Australian police built and distributed the replacement themselves, reading roughly 27 million messages from 12,000 devices before the takedown in June 2021. More than 800 arrests followed across 16 countries; the admissibility of the material has been litigated ever since.
cases.cite: US v. Iosif Florea et al., S.D. Cal., indictment June 2021; AFP Operation Ironside
cases.rank: Encrypted handset network — run by police (encrypted communications)
cases.drop_reason: Police building and running an encrypted phone network is a police operation against criminals, not infiltration.

cases.n: Ghost
cases.d: A platform sold with modified handsets and a remote wipe function, taken down in September 2024 with 51 arrests across Europe, Australia and North America. Its alleged administrator, who had run it from his parents' house in Sydney, was arrested there.
cases.cite: Europol and Eurojust coordinated action, September 2024; AFP charges
cases.drop_reason: A company selling encrypted phones to criminals is a sale of a product, not someone getting inside an institution.

cases.n: Matrix
cases.d: Found on a phone belonging to a man convicted of murdering a Dutch crime journalist, and taken down in December 2024 after French and Dutch investigators monitored it for three months and read 2.3 million messages. It ran on more than 40 servers and admitted users by invitation only.
cases.cite: Europol and Eurojust, Operation Passionflower, December 2024
cases.drop_reason: An encrypted service used by criminals and then monitored by police is not infiltration.

cases.n: Exclu
cases.d: Dutch and German police read the service for five months before closing it in February 2023, then raided a drug lab and two cocaine sites the messages had identified. Its operators were prosecuted in the Netherlands.
cases.cite: Dutch Politie and Europol action, February 2023; Netherlands prosecutions from 2023
cases.drop_reason: An encrypted service read by police and then closed is a police operation, not infiltration.

cases.n: Ennetcom
cases.d: The first of the European encrypted-phone takedowns: 19,000 handsets, servers seized in Canada, and an owner convicted of laundering and weapons offences. The recovered message store has been used in Dutch murder and trafficking trials for years since.
cases.cite: Dutch Openbaar Ministerie prosecution from April 2016; Rotterdam District Court conviction
cases.drop_reason: A company selling encrypted handsets to criminals is a product sale, not infiltration.

cases.n: Grupo Wisa and Balboa Bank & Trust
cases.d: A trading group in the Colon Free Zone, a duty-free retailer, a newspaper and a bank were designated together as a trade-based laundering network for several trafficking organisations. Panama's regulator seized the bank and wound it down; one of the designated principals later pleaded guilty in Miami to a bank-fraud conspiracy.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, May 2016; Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama seizure, 2016
cases.rank: Free-zone trading group and its bank (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: The record describes a designation of a family's laundering businesses and bank, not an outside party taking hidden control of an institution.

cases.n: Nemesis Market
cases.d: German police seized the market's servers in March 2024 and the US Treasury designated its administrator, an Iranian national, in a rare case of naming a market operator by name rather than only the platform. It had roughly 30,000 users and 1,000 vendors selling narcotics.
cases.cite: BKA seizure, March 2024; OFAC designation, March 2024
cases.drop_reason: A darknet market seizure and designation of its administrator; no one inside an institution.

cases.n: Endo International
cases.d: Agreed to about $450 million in opioid settlements through bankruptcy, having marketed a reformulated oxycodone as harder to abuse than the evidence supported. New York had already obtained a separate settlement over the same claims.
cases.cite: In re Endo International plc, S.D.N.Y. bankruptcy, settlement 2022; New York State settlement 2021
cases.drop_reason: A manufacturer's misleading marketing and settlement is its own conduct, not infiltration.

cases.n: Resorts World Las Vegas
cases.d: Settled a Nevada Gaming Control Board complaint for $10.5 million over hosting patrons with convictions for illegal bookmaking and money laundering, including one who had been barred from the state's casinos. Its president departed before the settlement was approved.
cases.cite: Nevada Gaming Commission settlement, 2025; Gaming Control Board complaint, 2024
cases.drop_reason: A casino hosting convicted bookmakers is a regulatory failure, not a crime group inside it.

cases.n: The Manta fishing fleet
cases.d: Fifteen Ecuador-based targets were designated on 20 August 2026 and ten fishing vessels identified as blocked property, over a network run out of Manta for Los Choneros and Los Lobos. The fleet does not carry the cocaine: it meets the go-fast boats at sea and supplies refuelling, food and medical assistance while watching for law enforcement, so a licensed vessel with a legitimate reason to be offshore becomes the service station for the crossing. Treasury noted the boats used government-subsidised fuel, which puts a state subsidy inside the cost structure of the route. One designated operator was said to coordinate 30 to 40 tonnes a month; another owned or controlled six companies, five of them in marine fishing. The Ecuadorian navy took 1.8 tonnes off a small fishing boat off Manabi in April 2026.
cases.cite: US Treasury press release sb0610 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended, 20 August 2026; Federal Register notice, 25 August 2026; Ecuadorian Ministry of National Defense seizure, 1 April 2026
cases.rank: Licensed tuna companies and ten blocked vessels (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A fishing fleet supplying smugglers at sea is smuggling support, with no one placed inside a government or company.

cases.n: Tapgas Mexico
cases.d: A Culiacan gas company designated with its owner, whose organisation Treasury says had laundered at least $16.5 million for Sinaloa Cartel clients including Los Chapitos and the Zambada faction. Fuel distribution moves cash volumes that would draw attention anywhere else.
cases.cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 2025
cases.rank: Fuel distribution — laundering vehicle (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A company designated for laundering cartel money is a front business, not an outside party inside an existing institution.

cases.n: Los Pochos company network
cases.d: Nine Guatemalan businesses have been designated across two actions as property of an organisation that controls trafficking on the Mexican border and supplies the Sinaloa Cartel. The companies are the part of the structure that survives a change of leadership, which is why Treasury relisted them.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, December 2019; E.O. 14059 designations, February 2024
cases.rank: Guatemalan trading and service companies (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Trafficking-owned businesses designated as property are front companies, not infiltration.

cases.n: Afghan hawala houses — the Barakzai network
cases.d: Two Kandahar exchange houses were designated with the opium network that used them, one belonging to the network's head and one to its main financial conduit. Hawala settles by ledger between brokers rather than by transfer, so there is no wire for a bank to screen and no correspondent to hold liable.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2012; Afghan Threat Finance Cell investigation
cases.rank: Money exchange houses — value transfer (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Exchange houses owned by an opium network are its own businesses, designated; no infiltration.

cases.n: Afghan and UAE trading companies — the Mohammad Din network
cases.d: Four companies in Afghanistan and the UAE were designated as vehicles for a Helmand heroin operation running labs in Musa Qala and Sangin. Dubai's role in the Afghan opiate economy is where the proceeds are placed rather than where the drug moves.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2014
cases.rank: Trading companies — proceeds placement (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Companies designated as vehicles for a heroin operation are fronts, not infiltration.

cases.n: Latakia captagon production
cases.d: Treasury identified a facility in the coastal province run by a presidential cousin as producing 84 million captagon tablets in 2020, coordinated with the Fourth Division and Hezbollah contacts. Manufacture at that volume needs presses, precursor supply and export clearance, which is why the map treats it as industry rather than as a lab.
cases.cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 13582, March 2023
cases.drop_reason: The record describes drug production run by the ruling family and army, with no outside party getting inside the state.

cases.n: Syrian private security companies
cases.d: The EU designated several private security companies as shells for pro-regime militias involved in the drug economy. The security licence is the cover: it explains armed men, vehicles and access to sites without any of it needing to be accounted for as military.
cases.cite: Council of the EU designations, April 2023
cases.rank: Security firms — militia shells (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Security companies used as shells by militias is a designation of fronts, not infiltration.

cases.n: The Joumaa exchange houses and used-car network
cases.d: Treasury designated a Lebanese-Colombian trafficker along with nine associates and 19 businesses, describing a system that moved as much as $200 million a month through exchange houses, bulk cash and used-car sales in the United States resold in West Africa. A Virginia indictment followed, charging the coordination of at least 85 tonnes of Colombian cocaine with Los Zetas. He has never been in US custody.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, January 2011; US v. Joumaa, E.D. Va., indictment November 2011
cases.rank: Money exchange houses and vehicle trading (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A trafficker's own exchange houses and car businesses designated is laundering, not infiltration.

cases.n: Operation Cedar — the luxury goods circuit
cases.d: Simultaneous raids in France, Belgium, Germany and Italy broke a laundering circuit that converted European cocaine proceeds into watches, cars and diamonds bought in Europe and resold in the Middle East. Goods carry value across borders without a wire transfer, which is the same mechanism the gold and used-car cases show.
cases.cite: DEA Operation Cedar, February 2016; French, Belgian, German and Italian prosecutions
cases.rank: Luxury goods trading — value transfer (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A laundering circuit through luxury goods purchases has no outside party inside an institution.

cases.n: The Khanani money laundering organisation
cases.d: A Karachi-based exchange group designated by Treasury as laundering for drug organisations, designated terrorist groups and Chinese and Colombian networks at once, on an estimated multi-billion-dollar annual scale. Its principal was arrested in Panama, extradited, and pleaded guilty in the United States in 2016.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, November 2015; US v. Khanani, D. Ariz., plea 2016
cases.rank: Exchange house group — multi-client laundering (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A laundering organisation designated and prosecuted for its own services is not infiltration.

cases.n: Tri-border free zone trading — the Barakat network
cases.d: Argentina froze the assets of a Ciudad del Este trading network in 2018 and the US designated its principals; the free zone's paperwork lets goods, invoices and value move without matching cargo. It sits at the junction of the Paraguayan cocaine corridor and the region's largest informal remittance market.
cases.cite: OFAC designations 2004 and 2018; Argentine Unidad de Informacion Financiera freezing order, 2018
cases.rank: Free trade zone import-export (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A trading network designated and frozen for laundering has no one placed inside an institution.

cases.n: The eight Wuhan and Hebei chemical companies
cases.d: Eight China-based companies and eight employees were indicted in Florida in October 2024 over synthetic opioids and fentanyl precursors, with the charges naming who held each firm's bitcoin wallet or received its Western Union payments. Five of the companies have since ceased operating and China scheduled three of the chemicals involved, which had not been controlled when the sales were made.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice, M.D. Fla., indictments unsealed October 2024
cases.rank: Chemical manufacture and export — sales agents and payment handlers (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: Chemical companies selling precursors is a sale of goods to criminals, not infiltration.

cases.n: Hubei Aoks Bio-Tech
cases.d: A Wuhan company, its sole director and three senior employees were charged in Los Angeles with conspiring to manufacture and distribute fentanyl and with selling precursors and xylazine worldwide. The misbranded-drug counts alongside the trafficking counts are the tell: the same shipments were being described to customs as something else.
cases.cite: US v. Hubei Aoks Bio-Tech Co. Ltd., C.D. Cal., indictment November 2024
cases.rank: Chemical manufacture — director and senior staff (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: A company selling precursors and misdescribing shipments is its own crime, not infiltration.

cases.n: Vasudha Pharma Chem
cases.d: An Indian company and senior executives were indicted after selling an undercover agent 25 kilograms of a listed fentanyl precursor twice, then negotiating four tonnes of it — half destined for Sinaloa, half for the United States — for about $380,000. It had advertised the chemicals openly on its website and at trade shows.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice and DEA, indictment announced March 2025
cases.drop_reason: A company offering precursors for sale openly is a sale to criminals, not infiltration.

cases.n: Chinese precursor vendors and crypto payment
cases.d: Blockchain tracing puts inflows to Chinese precursor vendors at roughly $31 million in 2023, $35 million in 2024 and $39 million in 2025, with about 97 percent accepting cryptocurrency and most marketing xylazine or nitazenes alongside the precursors. A 2026 indictment of Shandong suppliers added a material-support-to-a-terrorist-organisation count, available because Mexican cartels were designated in February 2025.
cases.cite: US indictment of Shandong-based suppliers, 2026; TRM Labs blockchain analysis, 2026
cases.rank: Online precursor marketplaces — payment rails (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: Vendors selling precursors for crypto is a sale of goods, not infiltration.

cases.n: Law firm escrow accounts — the Ravenell case
cases.d: A prominent Baltimore defence lawyer was convicted after a 16-day trial of using his firm's escrow and operating accounts to move more than a million dollars in drug proceeds, pay counsel for other members of the conspiracy, and invest on a trafficker client's behalf. He was sentenced to 57 months. Escrow is the one account a lawyer can hold for a client without explaining whose money it is.
cases.cite: US v. Ravenell, D. Md., verdict December 2021, sentence June 2022
cases.rank: Defence counsel — client trust account (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A lawyer laundering for his own client is his own crime; the record does not show an outside party placing or controlling anyone inside an institution.

cases.n: Chinese money laundering organisations
cases.d: Brokers who buy cartel cash in the United States at a discount and settle in China through mirror transfers have largely displaced the older Colombian peso exchange. Prosecutions in North Carolina, Georgia and Virginia have produced sentences of six to fifteen years and forfeitures in the tens of millions; the demand side is Chinese nationals needing dollars abroad, which is what makes the service cheap.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice, W.D.N.C. sentence 2026; E.D. Va. sentences 2024–2025; DEA National Drug Threat Assessment
cases.rank: Informal brokers — cash collection and mirror transfer (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Money brokers buying cartel cash is a laundering service, not infiltration of an institution.

cases.n: Sham technology company — the Bibliowicz case
cases.d: A senior executive was convicted by a Brooklyn jury of laundering more than $300 million for cartels including Sinaloa, routed behind a technology company that existed to explain the flows. He was sentenced to 12 years with a $330 million forfeiture judgment.
cases.cite: US v. Bibliowicz Mitrani, E.D.N.Y., verdict December 2025, sentence April 2026
cases.rank: Corporate executive — unlicensed money transmission (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A sham company set up to launder cartel money is a front, not an outside party inside an existing institution.

cases.n: High-value freight forwarders — the jewellery corridor
cases.d: An organisation working from a jewellery-store front in the Los Angeles Jewelry Mart shipped locked cases of cocaine to New York's Diamond District through forwarders that specialise in precious metals and fine art, and sent the cash back the same way. At least 1,300 parcels moved between the two cities. Carriers built for high-value goods offer sealed handling and few questions.
cases.cite: US v. Rodriguez, O'Connell and others, C.D. Cal., superseding indictment 2025
cases.rank: Specialist parcel carriers — jewellery and fine art (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: Smugglers using freight forwarders as customers is smuggling, with no insider shown.

cases.n: Airport ground handling — the NAHCO case
cases.d: A cargo manager at Nigeria's main aviation handling company pleaded guilty to stealing and trafficking 25 kilograms of ephedrine from the import shed inside the customs area at Lagos airport, and was sentenced to three years. Ground handling sits on the airside of every control and is rarely counted as part of the supply chain.
cases.cite: Federal High Court Lagos, NDLEA prosecution, conviction December 2025
cases.rank: Cargo handling company — import shed manager (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A cargo manager stealing ephedrine is an insider's own crime; the record names no outside party.

cases.n: Sahel gold and real estate — laundering the cocaine surge
cases.d: Cocaine seizures across Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger rose from an average of 13 kilograms a year between 2015 and 2020 to 1,466 kilograms in 2022, and Mauritania alone took 2.3 tonnes by mid-2023. The UN found the proceeds moving into gold and real estate, sectors growing fast enough to absorb them, and named armed groups in Mali among the beneficiaries. No prosecution has followed in any of the five states.
cases.cite: UNODC, Drug Trafficking in the Sahel, April 2024
cases.rank: Artisanal gold buyers and property developers (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Drug proceeds moving into gold and property is laundering, with no one placed inside an institution.

cases.n: The adulterated fuel chain
cases.d: Methanol entered through the port of Paranagua on falsified paperwork, was diverted to blenders who mixed it into petrol, and reached consumers through stations the organisation controlled. Prosecutors put illicit fuel imports at 10 billion reais and retail sales at 52 billion. Buyers were defrauded twice over, on volume and on specification, which is the rare instance on this map where the laundering vehicle harms the public directly rather than only carrying the proceeds.
cases.cite: Operacao Carbono Oculto findings, Receita Federal and ANP, 2025
cases.rank: Fuel importers, blenders and retail stations (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: The record describes a fuel fraud and laundering scheme by the organisation itself; the infiltration angle of the same operation is carried by the Carbono Oculto entry.

cases.n: The Shimada network and the leaked raid
cases.d: Two Brazilians, three Brazilian companies and one Portuguese company were designated on 1 July 2026 over a laundering network running between Florida and Sao Paulo. Treasury put the sum at more than $30 million generated in US cities and moved back to Brazil in cryptocurrency; the FBI had already arrested six of the Florida node in January 2026. One of the designated companies had surfaced a year earlier in a laundering network tied to a Sao Paulo football club whose agent was said to work for the PCC. What happened next is the record: Brazil's federal police had a parallel operation ready, and their chief said the uncoordinated US designation forced them to execute their warrants earlier than planned. The associate was captured; the principal escaped and is a fugitive.
cases.cite: US Treasury press release sb0549 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224 as amended, 1 July 2026; FBI arrests and indictment, S.D. Fla., January 2026; Brazilian Federal Police Operation Exchange and statements by the Federal Police director, July 2026
cases.rank: Payment and trading companies moving proceeds in crypto (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: The record covers a designation and its clash with a Brazilian operation; the only insider link (a club agent said to work for the PCC) is too thin to carry the entry.

cases.n: The Hong Pang Group
cases.d: Founded in 1998 with drug revenues under the privileges of a ceasefire deal, the group spread into construction, agriculture, gems and minerals, petroleum, electronics and department stores, with offices in Yangon, Mandalay and Lashio as well as Wa territory. Treasury designated 16 companies in 2005 and a further 17 with 26 individuals in 2008 as the commercial network of the United Wa State Army; US prosecutors sought $103 million in forfeitures tied to the group. It later traded under a different name and its founder remains a fugitive.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, November 2005 and November 2008; US v. Wei Hsueh Kang and others, E.D.N.Y., indictment unsealed January 2005
cases.rank: Conglomerate — construction, mining, gems, fuel, retail (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Companies owned by an armed group as its commercial arm are its own businesses, designated, not infiltration.

cases.n: The Menu-Based Sanctions list — a head of state without an asset freeze
cases.d: Haiti's former president was placed on the Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions list rather than the main blocking list, which prohibits foreign-exchange transactions and bars US financial institutions from lending to him without freezing his property outright. The distinction matters for what a designation actually does: the graduated tier reaches banking relationships while leaving assets untouched, and it is the tier chosen for a designated former head of state.
cases.cite: OFAC Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions listing under E.O. 14059, August 2024
cases.rank: Sanctions instrument rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: The record explains a sanctions listing tier and does not describe any infiltration.

cases.n: ENACO — the legal coca monopoly
cases.d: Peru's state company holds the sole legal right to buy and sell coca leaf, registering around 31,000 producers and exporting to a US firm that extracts cocaine for medical use. Researchers examining the country's main legal coca valley found the monopoly pays below what traffickers offer, so most of the crop leaves the legal channel it was designed to capture. It is the one entry on this map where the state itself is the licensed buyer of the raw material.
cases.cite: Busnel and Manrique Lopez, International Journal on Drug Policy, 2023; ENACO producer registry
cases.rank: State coca purchasing monopoly (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A state coca monopoly underpaying farmers is a policy issue, not infiltration.

cases.n: Singapore's drug-proceeds statute in practice
cases.d: Thirty-two men were convicted in 2025 alone under the Confiscation of Benefits Act, which makes possessing or moving the proceeds of drug dealing a separate offence from trafficking. The largest single laundering sentence, 38 months within a 28-year term, concerned removing about S$1.27 million from the jurisdiction. The sums are small by the standards of every bank on this layer, and the sentences are not: the same conduct that draws a corporate fine elsewhere draws imprisonment and caning here.
cases.cite: Singapore Central Narcotics Bureau convictions, 2024 and 2025; Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992
cases.rank: Statutory regime — possession and transfer of drug benefits (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Convictions under a drug-proceeds law describe enforcement, not infiltration.

cases.n: The tapentadol export pipeline
cases.d: More than 60 Indian suppliers exported roughly $130 million of tapentadol pills to West African countries that had not approved the drug, at doses above the Indian manufacturing cap. Regulators had seized one manufacturer's stock and halted production after an earlier investigation; exports of the same opioid then rose. A regulator's own reply named only two firms as approved to make tapentadol for export in 2019-2024, and neither appears among the 60. Around 30 percent of West Africa's population is estimated to use tramadol or codeine.
cases.cite: Bellingcat and Newslaundry investigation, April 2026; CDSCO records obtained under RTI; BBC Eye investigation, February 2025
cases.drop_reason: Manufacturers exporting unapproved opioids is a sales and regulation issue, not infiltration.

cases.n: Online pharmacies and counterfeit pills
cases.d: Treasury designated an Indian online pharmacy and two nationals who worked with Dominican and US traffickers to sell counterfeit pills marketed as discounted legitimate medication and filled instead with illicit fentanyl. The same online suppliers sell precursor chemicals to Mexican laboratories, so one channel serves both the finished counterfeit and the raw material for it.
cases.cite: OFAC designations, September 2025; DEA public warning, October 2024
cases.drop_reason: An online pharmacy selling counterfeit pills is a sale to buyers, not infiltration.

cases.n: Kings Romans casino
cases.d: Treasury designated the casino and its owner's organisation in January 2018, stating it was used to store and distribute narcotics from Myanmar's United Wa State Army and to launder the proceeds, with drug seizures in Thailand, Laos and China traced back to it since 2014. The owner denied the allegations at a press conference within days. The casino kept operating and expanding, which is the clearest single measure on this map of what a designation is worth inside a jurisdiction that will not act on it.
cases.cite: OFAC Transnational Criminal Organizations designation, January 2018; subsequent UNODC reporting on the Golden Triangle SEZ
cases.rank: Casino — storage, distribution and laundering (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: A casino openly owned by a designated criminal organisation is its own business; no one got inside an outside institution.

cases.n: The Mekong casino banking system
cases.d: UNODC counted more than 340 licensed and unlicensed casinos across the lower Mekong by early 2022, and describes them with online gambling and stablecoin transfers as a parallel banking system handling proceeds from drug trafficking, illegal gambling and cyberfraud. The displacement is documented: enforcement against Macau's junkets moved the business into Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and the Philippines, and operations there moved it again toward border and remote areas. Treasury designations in Cambodia have reached casino complexes and two banks connected to them.
cases.cite: UNODC, Casinos, Money Laundering, Underground Banking and Transnational Organized Crime in East and Southeast Asia, January 2024; OFAC designations in Cambodia, 2025-2026
cases.rank: Licensed and unlicensed casinos, e-junkets (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: Casinos acting as underground banks is laundering and weak regulation, with no specific insider placement shown.

cases.n: Operation BULUT and the afterlife of seized message stores
cases.d: Coordinated raids across several European states and Turkiye in April 2025 produced 232 arrests and more than 300 million euros in assets, worked out of Sky ECC and ANOM material years after both platforms were closed. Europol's operations deputy said the archives are still turning intelligence into action. The corollary sits in the same reporting: rather than ending encrypted communication, the takedowns fragmented it into smaller bespoke services, so each seizure buys an archive rather than a market.
cases.cite: Europol and national authorities, Operation BULUT, April 2025
cases.rank: Archived platform data — four dismantled services (encrypted communications)
cases.drop_reason: Raids based on seized police message archives are law enforcement, not infiltration.

cases.n: Tirana high-rises and coastal land
cases.d: Albania's special prosecution issued 20 arrest warrants and seized over 100 million euros in assets, tracing cocaine proceeds into land fraud along the coastline and into high-rise towers under construction in the capital. Its seizure order records the central figure planning shipments at meetings in Spain, Monaco, Germany and Aruba, and refers to meetings with senior Albanian state officials whom it does not name. Among the implicated plots is land designated for a resort promoted by US investors.
cases.cite: Albanian Special Prosecution (SPAK) asset seizure order and arrest warrants, 2026; BIRN analysis of the investigative file
cases.rank: Property development and land transactions (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: The record describes laundering into property; its only official link is unnamed meetings, too thin to show infiltration.

cases.n: The Hysa network — casinos and restaurants in Mexico
cases.d: Treasury designated 27 individuals and entities in November 2025 over a Mexico-based laundering scheme run by an Albanian family working with the Sinaloa Cartel, washing drug proceeds through casinos and luxury restaurants in Sinaloa, Sonora and other states. Separately, an independent Albanian trafficker is alleged to have moved over $31 million through Ecuador's financial system using front companies between 2015 and 2024.
cases.cite: OFAC designations, November 2025; Ecuadorian prosecution filings; InSight Crime analysis, 2026
cases.rank: Casinos and restaurants — placement (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A family laundering through its own casinos and restaurants is laundering, not infiltration of an outside institution.

cases.n: Sutaria, SR Chemicals and Agrat Chemicals
cases.d: An India-based pharmaceutical chemicals supplier and his salesperson used two chemical companies to ship fentanyl precursors to Mexico and Guatemala, including N-Boc-4-Piperidone, mislabelled as safe chemicals. Both were arrested by Indian authorities in March 2025 and designated on 23 April 2026 within a 23-target action against a procurement network serving the Sinaloa Cartel. US estimates put a kilogram of the precursor at roughly 1.83 kilograms of fentanyl. Treasury's framing is the significant part: cartels now synthesise from precursors imported mainly from Asia rather than refining plant material, so the chemical broker sits where the grower used to, and the offence itself is a description on a shipping document.
cases.cite: US Treasury press release sb0468 and OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026; Indian arrests, March 2025; US Department of Justice yield estimates
cases.rank: Pharmaceutical chemical suppliers shipping mislabelled precursors (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: Chemical firms shipping mislabelled precursors is smuggling, not infiltration.

cases.n: Cartok and Carhern — the precursor brokers' companies
cases.d: Two Sinaloa companies owned by a married pair of precursor brokers were designated in April 2026. One was linked to seizures of 1-Boc-4-Hydroxypiperidine totalling over 50 kilograms; her husband, a fentanyl and cocaine supplier with family ties to the Chapitos faction, used launderers inside the United States to collect drug payments. Both were arrested in Mexico in March 2026, a month before the designation.
cases.cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026; Mexican arrests, March 2026
cases.rank: Trading companies owned by designated brokers (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: Brokers' own companies designated for precursor dealing are fronts, not infiltration.

cases.n: Reyma and Aduaeasy — customs brokerage
cases.d: Two firms handling importation and customs clearance were designated in the same April 2026 action for materially contributing to the proliferation of illicit drugs. The customs broker is the least visible link in the precursor chain: the chemical is legal to ship, the paperwork decides whether anyone looks at it, and the broker writes the paperwork.
cases.cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 14059, 23 April 2026
cases.rank: Freight forwarding and customs clearance (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: Customs brokers designated for contributing to drug flows; the record does not show anyone placed or paid inside an institution.

cases.n: The Ochoa Vasco front companies
cases.d: Treasury designated 15 entities and nine individuals as the front network of a Colombian trafficker already listed in 2007, spanning Colombia, Mexico and the Caribbean. A Guadalajara cluster controlled by his front man included an agricultural company and three construction and property firms. The pattern recurs across this layer: the fronts are ordinary businesses in unglamorous sectors, chosen because nothing about them invites a question.
cases.cite: OFAC designations under E.O. 12978, 2011
cases.rank: Agriculture, construction and real estate fronts (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Front companies designated for a trafficker are his own businesses, not infiltration.

cases.n: Chams money laundering organisation
cases.d: Designated by Treasury in April 2019 as a laundering organisation serving trafficking groups, and issued as one of OFAC's named press charts alongside the Zheng fentanyl network and the Peralta organisation. Naming the launderer separately from the traffickers it serves is the shift this layer records: the service is a business with its own clients rather than an arm of any one cartel.
cases.cite: OFAC designation, April 2019; OFAC counter-narcotics press chart, Chams Money Laundering Organization
cases.rank: Peso exchange and value transfer (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A laundering organisation designated for its services is not infiltration.

cases.n: GOLDPHARMA — the mail-order pill network
cases.d: Designated by Treasury in May 2019 as a drug trafficking organisation running internet pharmacies that shipped controlled substances by post to buyers worldwide. It is the earliest entry on this layer treating an online pharmacy as a trafficking organisation rather than a regulatory problem, a framing the Indian counterfeit-pill designations of 2025 follow directly.
cases.cite: OFAC designation, May 2019; OFAC counter-narcotics press chart, GOLDPHARMA Drug Trafficking Organization
cases.rank: Online pharmacy network — mail-order controlled substances (pharmaceutical supply)
cases.drop_reason: An online pharmacy network designated as a trafficking group is selling drugs, not infiltration.

cases.n: Dragon Secure GmbH — Kraden and Skyda
cases.d: A Zug-registered software company operating two encrypted messaging brands was designated under the illicit-drugs order in December 2024. Registering as an ordinary Swiss programming firm with a public website is a departure from the handset-based services this map records elsewhere: the product is an app rather than a modified phone, and the company is incorporated where its clients' proceeds are banked.
cases.cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 17 December 2024
cases.rank: Encrypted messaging software company (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: A software firm selling encrypted messaging to criminals is a product sale, not infiltration.

cases.n: Atiya S.A.S. — Medellin property
cases.d: A Medellin real estate company incorporated in May 2020 was designated in December 2024 as controlled by a Lithuanian national listed in the same action. Its stated business is holding property on its own or leased account, which is the whole utility: a company that only owns buildings generates no transactions to examine.
cases.cite: OFAC designation under E.O. 14059, 17 December 2024
cases.rank: Real estate holding company (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A property company owned by a designated trafficker is a front, not infiltration.

cases.n: Mexican cartel crude oil smuggling
cases.d: Treasury issued a dedicated advisory chart in May 2025 on cartel crude oil smuggling, mapping how stolen and mislabelled Mexican crude is moved and resold across the border as a revenue stream running parallel to narcotics. The same organisations that need precursor chemicals in also need value out, and a barrel of crude launders more cleanly than a wire.
cases.cite: OFAC counter-narcotics advisory and press chart, Mexican Cartel Crude Oil Smuggling Schemes, May 2025
cases.rank: Fuel theft, transport and cross-border resale (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Cartel crude oil smuggling is smuggling, with no insider shown in the record.

cases.n: Guyana as a transshipment point — the 2025 chart
cases.d: Treasury published a dedicated chart in June 2025 setting out how traffickers use Guyana to move cocaine toward the United States, alongside the designations of two domestic organisations, a serving police officer and Colombians running the airstrips. Publishing a country-level route chart rather than a single network diagram is unusual, and marks the point at which Guyana was treated as infrastructure rather than as a series of incidents.
cases.cite: OFAC counter-narcotics chart, Traffickers Use Guyana as a Cocaine Transshipment Point to the U.S., June 2025
cases.rank: Airstrips, river craft and port clearance (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A route chart and designations describe smuggling; the record does not develop the single police officer into an infiltration case.

cases.n: The Grajales company group
cases.d: A Valle del Cauca family's cluster of agro-industrial and holding companies sat on the sanctions list for years before being removed in December 2020. The map carries it because delisting is the part of this instrument that leaves no trace: the designation is announced with a press release, the removal appears as a line in a technical update, and the businesses resume.
cases.cite: OFAC SDN List deletions, 2 December 2020; original SDNT designations under E.O. 12978
cases.rank: Agro-industrial and holding companies — delisting record (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A delisted family company group is a note on sanctions procedure, not infiltration.

cases.n: Zaron Bio-Tech (Asia) Limited
cases.d: A chemical company registered in Hong Kong and operating out of the Shanghai region, designated in April 2018 as owned or controlled by a fentanyl trafficker indicted in North Dakota for running a continuing criminal enterprise. It produces food additives and operates factories in China, Vietnam, Thailand and Singapore, and was used to move fentanyl and analogues into the United States. Four associates were designated for laundering the proceeds through money service businesses.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, April 2018; US v. Zhang, D.N.D., indictment unsealed October 2017
cases.rank: Food additives manufacturer — fentanyl shipment (chemicals & precursors)
cases.drop_reason: A chemical company owned by a trafficker and used to ship fentanyl is smuggling, not infiltration.

cases.n: Emerald mining fronts — the Rincon Castillo network
cases.d: Treasury identified a Colombian organisation and its associated entities in June 2018, among them emerald mining companies and the Envigado Futbol Club. Gemstones and a football club share a property useful to the trade: both carry large cash flows whose valuation is a matter of opinion rather than record.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act identification, 5 June 2018; Congressional Research Service overview of narcotics sanctions, 2018
cases.rank: Emerald mining and a football club (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Mining companies and a football club designated as a network's entities; the record does not show hidden control of an outside institution.

cases.n: La Oficina de Envigado — the enforcement service
cases.d: Designated under the Kingpin Act in June 2014, with a laundering network, an underboss and ten individuals and fourteen entities designated across the following weeks. Treasury's description is what places it here: the group supplies other criminal networks with enforcement services, debt collection, extortion and murder for hire. Eight further underbosses were designated in September, several of them coordinating from inside Colombian prisons.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, June, July and September 2014
cases.rank: Debt collection, extortion and contract violence sold as a service (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A criminal group selling enforcement services and designated is not infiltration of an institution.

cases.n: The Mejia Salazar laundering network
cases.d: Designated in July 2014 with members of his network for laundering narcotics proceeds on behalf of La Oficina de Envigado, one week after that group's own designation. The sequencing is the point: the enforcement arm and its launderer were treated as separate businesses with a client relationship rather than as one organisation.
cases.cite: OFAC designations as Specially Designated Narcotics Traffickers, 1 July 2014
cases.rank: Laundering service to a single client organisation (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A launderer designated for serving a criminal group is not infiltration.

cases.n: Los Valles organisation
cases.d: Designated in August 2014 as one of the most prolific Central American trafficking organisations, moving cocaine north through Honduras. It sits alongside the Cachiros and the Rosenthal group already on this map: three Honduran networks designated within a year of one another, each with a legitimate business face and each connected to officials the map records separately.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, 20 August 2014
cases.rank: Family trafficking organisation and its holdings (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A trafficking organisation designated; the record does not describe its links to officials.

cases.n: Five companies at one Medellin address
cases.d: Treasury designated four Colombians and five companies in May 2017 as ultimately owned or directed by a La Oficina de Envigado financier through front persons. The companies span estate planning, coffee, mining and meat trading, and all five are registered at a single office in Medellin. It was the seventh OFAC action against the same organisation, which is what the layer records: the fronts are replaced faster than they are designated.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, May 2017; OFAC press chart, Gallon Henao Brothers' Business Partners and Companies
cases.rank: Estate planning, coffee production, mining and meat trading (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Front companies at one address are a trafficker's own businesses, not infiltration.

cases.n: Semillanos S.A. — the Cordoba farm
cases.d: An agricultural company based at Cerete in Cordoba, with a hacienda five kilometres out of town, designated in June 2015 as owned or controlled by a financier of La Oficina de Envigado. Farmland absorbs money in a way few assets do: the yield is variable, the inputs are cash, and the valuation depends on a harvest nobody audits.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designation, June 2015
cases.rank: Agricultural company and estate (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A farm company owned by a financier is a front, not infiltration.

cases.n: The Ruano Yandun fleet
cases.d: A Narino-based organisation designated in November 2017 for moving multi-ton cocaine loads from Colombia and Ecuador through Central America and Mexico using speedboats, fishing vessels and self-propelled semi-submersibles. Treasury named it a key contributor to the rise in cocaine production in Narino, which is the department the Colombian coca figures turn on.
cases.cite: OFAC Kingpin Act designations, November 2017
cases.rank: Speedboats, fishing vessels and semi-submersibles (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A smuggling organisation using boats is smuggling, not infiltration.

cases.n: Javier Garcia Rojas and four Colombian companies
cases.d: Three Colombians and four companies they own or direct were designated in 2018 for links to La Oficina de Envigado and to a financier designated in 2016. Treasury's stated ground is unusual on this layer: the men were targeted for attempts to undermine joint US-Colombian investigations rather than for moving drugs or money. It was OFAC's eighth action against the same organisation since its designation on 26 June 2014, which is the pattern these Medellin entries record together — the fronts are replaced about as fast as they are named.
cases.cite: US Treasury press release sm0289, OFAC Kingpin Act designations, 2018; La Oficina de Envigado designated 26 June 2014
cases.rank: Companies held by men accused of obstructing the investigation (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Front companies designated for obstructing investigations; the record shows no one inside an institution.

cases.n: The Los Gueros business network
cases.d: Six companies and five individuals were designated in September 2013 as the business network of a Guadalajara organisation within the Sinaloa Cartel, three years after the group and its four leader brothers were listed in February 2011. Treasury's finding is the method: by using aliases and putting close family members and associates on the company deeds, the group hid its ownership interest in companies and properties for many years. The designations followed the extradition of two leaders, charged in Brooklyn over an organisation alleged to have imported more than 100,000 kilograms of cocaine between 1996 and 2008. The holdings include a fuel and mining company, an early instance of Treasury naming fuel as a trafficking asset.
cases.cite: US Treasury press releases tg1043 (February 2011) and jl2170 (September 2013), OFAC Kingpin Act designations; indictment E.D.N.Y., 2009; DEA statement, 24 September 2013
cases.rank: Six companies held through relatives and associates (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: A cartel hiding ownership of its own companies through relatives is laundering through fronts, not getting inside an outside institution.

cases.n: Gold bars in an Italian house
cases.d: Proceeds from drug trafficking in France were collected at a residence in Italy and converted into gold bars and sheets, then carried on to Kosovo, Turkiye and Morocco. Investigators put at least 18 million euros through the scheme in ten months and seized about 31 million in assets across two operations. A couple is under investigation in Italy for running it. Gold crosses a border as an object rather than a transaction.
cases.cite: Eurojust and Europol coordinated operations with French, Italian and Kosovar authorities, September 2025 and June 2026
cases.rank: Cash-to-gold conversion and transport (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Converting drug cash into gold is laundering, not infiltration.

cases.n: Fake invoices between France and Romania
cases.d: A network laundering 306 million euros of drug and tax-evasion proceeds through front companies and real estate was broken up in February 2026 with thirteen arrests and 24 house searches. Invoices for services never performed moved money between the two countries and cut the taxable income at the same time, so a single false document does the laundering and the evasion together.
cases.cite: Eurojust and Europol joint investigation team, French and Romanian authorities, action day 3 February 2026
cases.rank: Corporate front companies and fictitious services (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Fake invoices between front companies is laundering and tax evasion, not infiltration.

cases.n: A laundering service with a client list
cases.d: Twenty-three people were arrested in January 2025 running a scheme that had laundered around 100 million euros. Prosecutors described the group as acting as a financial service for other criminals to launder their profits, which is the distinction this layer keeps returning to: the launderer is a business with customers rather than a department inside any one trafficking group.
cases.cite: Eurojust coordinated investigation, arrests January 2025
cases.rank: Financial service sold to other criminal groups (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A laundering service for criminals is a criminal business, not infiltration.

cases.n: Shell companies for the Camorra and 'Ndrangheta
cases.d: French, Italian and Swiss authorities followed suspicious financial movements to a laundering operation serving members of both the Camorra and the 'Ndrangheta, using shell companies, false invoicing and luxury investments to clean millions in cocaine profits. A Belgian customs seizure in late 2025 tied the money back to the shipments. Two organisations that compete in the drug market shared the same laundering service.
cases.cite: Eurojust and Europol, French, Italian and Swiss investigation; arrest of the high-value target and six others, 2026
cases.rank: Shell companies, false invoicing and luxury investments (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: A shared laundering service for two mafias using shell companies is laundering, not infiltration.

cases.n: Lithuanian property and the Icelandic route
cases.d: A group moving cocaine, MDMA, ketamine and methamphetamine into Iceland laundered the revenue through real estate and other property in Lithuania. Twenty-four arrests were made across five countries in February 2026 with 41 house searches. The quantities are small by this map's standards and the structure is not: a retail trade at one end of Europe funding a property portfolio at the other.
cases.cite: Eurojust coordinated action day, arrests in Iceland, Lithuania, Spain, Belgium and Denmark, February 2026
cases.rank: Real estate as the destination for retail drug revenue (gold, commodities & agribusiness)
cases.drop_reason: Laundering drug money through property in Lithuania; no one placed inside an institution.

cases.n: Adapted vehicles out of Brussels
cases.d: Belgian and French authorities broke up a network in June 2026 that prepared vehicles with hidden compartments and ran consignments out of France and Belgium into Italy and Spain. Eleven arrests, 60,000 euros in cash and several vehicles seized. Europol estimates half of the most threatening criminal networks in the EU are involved in the drug trade, which is the context for treating a garage as trafficking infrastructure.
cases.cite: Eurojust coordinated operation, Belgian and French authorities, June 2026
cases.rank: Vehicle preparation with concealed compartments (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A smuggling network fitting hidden compartments in vehicles; no institution infiltrated.

cases.n: Vlissingen, Rotterdam and the Los Lobos consignments
cases.d: A joint Ecuadorian, Belgian and Dutch operation dismantled a network shipping for Ecuador's Los Lobos, with seizures including 1.1 tonnes at Rotterdam in June 2025 and over three tonnes in Belgium, and sixteen arrests on the action day. It is the same corridor the Manta fishing fleet designations describe from the loading end, recorded here at the port of arrival.
cases.cite: Europol-supported joint operation, Ecuador, Belgium and the Netherlands, 2025-2026
cases.rank: Container terminals and importer companies (shipping, freight & ports)
cases.drop_reason: A cocaine shipping network and seizures; no insider or captured institution named.

cases.n: The Belgian cocaine laboratory
cases.d: Fourteen arrests across Belgium, Germany and Italy in April 2025, over 780 kilograms of cocaine seized and an underground laboratory dismantled. The paste was shipped from Colombia and refined inside the European Union rather than at origin, which moves a step of production across the Atlantic and puts the chemist alongside the importer.
cases.cite: Europol-supported joint operation, Belgian and Italian authorities, April 2025
cases.drop_reason: A drug laboratory and arrests; ordinary trafficking with no institution infiltrated.

cases.n: Scottish network logistics
cases.d: Thirteen suspects from a Scottish organised crime group were arrested in March 2026 over the transport of hundreds of kilograms of cocaine, in an action coordinated from Eurojust rather than domestically. A domestic British group appearing on a European coordination docket is the point: the logistics arm is the part that crosses borders and so the part that draws a joint investigation team.
cases.cite: Eurojust coordinated joint action day, 27 March 2026
cases.rank: Transport arrangement for bulk consignments (lawyers, brokers & formation agents)
cases.drop_reason: Arrests of a Scottish gang over cocaine transport; no institution infiltrated.

cases.n: OKX
cases.d: The exchange pleaded guilty in 2025 to operating an unlicensed money transmitting business without registering with FinCEN, and agreed to pay more than $504 million. It is among the largest anti-money-laundering resolutions on record and belongs on this layer for the same reason the mixers do: a venue that moves value without identifying its users serves whoever needs that service.
cases.cite: US guilty plea and penalty, 2025
cases.rank: Exchange — unlicensed money transmission (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: A crypto exchange fined for running without a licence and weak money-laundering checks; no outside party inside it.

cases.n: KuCoin (PEKEN Global Limited)
cases.d: A $297 million penalty for failing to implement effective anti-money-laundering measures and to report suspicious transactions, with executives separately indicted in the United States over the Bank Secrecy Act and unlicensed money transmission. The exchange was registered in the Seychelles while serving customers in jurisdictions where it was not licensed.
cases.cite: US penalty and executive indictments, 2025
cases.rank: Exchange — suspicious transaction reporting (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: A crypto exchange fined for weak money-laundering controls; no outside party inside it.

cases.n: The 2025 enforcement gap
cases.d: US anti-money-laundering and sanctions penalties fell to about $1.7 billion in 2025, a 61 percent drop from $4.3 billion the year before, and for the first time in more than two decades not one US bank faced a major penalty in these categories. Enforcement shifted toward crypto and toward individual prosecutions. This layer records institutions penalised for moving drug proceeds; the year in which the banks were not penalised is part of that record.
cases.cite: Fenergo and Kroll compilations of 2025 penalties; FinCEN and DOJ policy statements, 2025
cases.rank: Regulatory pattern rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Statistics on falling US enforcement penalties, not a case of infiltration.

cases.n: Paxos Trust Company
cases.d: Fined $26.5 million by New York regulators for failing to monitor illicit flows from a partner exchange. The finding reaches the layer beneath the exchange: the issuer of the token was held responsible for what the venue distributing it did with it.
cases.cite: New York Department of Financial Services consent order, 2025
cases.rank: Stablecoin issuer — partner monitoring (crypto & digital rails)
cases.drop_reason: A token issuer fined for weak monitoring; no outside party inside it.

cases.n: Platinum Gaming and ProgressPlay
cases.d: The UK Gambling Commission fined one operator 10 million pounds in October 2025 over gaps in anti-money-laundering and safer gambling controls, and another 1 million pounds in August for failing to verify player funds and monitor high-risk accounts. Regulators have said gambling operators must apply the same customer due diligence standards as banks; the fines are what the gap between the two costs.
cases.cite: UK Gambling Commission penalties, August and October 2025
cases.rank: Online gambling operators — source of funds checks (casinos & junkets)
cases.drop_reason: Gambling operators fined for weak money-laundering checks; no crime group shown inside them.

cases.n: The FATF blacklist — three countries
cases.d: Only Iran, North Korea and Myanmar sit on the FATF list subject to a call for action, unchanged since Myanmar was added in October 2022. All three appear in this map's other layers, and the overlap is the finding: the jurisdictions the global standard-setter treats as beyond monitoring are the same ones where no official has ever been prosecuted for drug capture.
cases.cite: FATF public statement, high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action, February 2026 plenary
cases.rank: Jurisdiction-level listing rather than a firm (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: A FATF blacklisting of countries, not a case of anyone getting inside an institution.

cases.n: The grey list and its exits
cases.d: Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Nigeria and South Africa were removed from FATF's increased-monitoring list in October 2025, South Africa after only two years. Kuwait and Papua New Guinea were added in February 2026. Each of the four exits is a country this map records for capture cases or protected corridors, so a compliance clearance and a prosecution record can move in opposite directions at the same time.
cases.cite: FATF plenary outcomes, October 2025 and February 2026
cases.rank: Increased-monitoring listing and delisting (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Countries leaving a FATF monitoring list, not a case of infiltration.

cases.n: Bolivia and the British Virgin Islands listings
cases.d: Both were added to FATF's increased-monitoring list in June 2025, in the same session that removed Croatia, Mali and Tanzania. The pairing is instructive: a cocaine-producing state and an offshore company registry listed together, at opposite ends of the same chain.
cases.cite: FATF plenary outcome, 13 June 2025
cases.rank: Jurisdictions added to increased monitoring (banks & money transmission)
cases.drop_reason: Countries added to a FATF monitoring list, not a case of infiltration.

cases.n: Laos and Nepal listings
cases.d: Added in February 2025, in the session that removed the Philippines after four years of reform. Laos also holds the Golden Triangle special economic zone and the designated casino this map records separately, so the listing reaches the banking system of a state that granted the concession.
cases.cite: FATF plenary outcome, 21 February 2025
cases.rank: Jurisdictions added to increased monitoring (banks & money transmission)
