orgs.d: Swedish tobacco company (snus), bought by Philip Morris International in 2022. An approach to it seeking €60 million for help with EU tobacco rules led to the departure of EU Health Commissioner John Dalli in 2012.
orgs.drop_reason: Swedish Match was the target of a request for money, not the party getting inside the EU; the record shows no infiltration by the company.

orgs.n: Erik Prince security companies (Blackwater, Frontier Services Group, Vectus Global)
orgs.d: Erik Prince founded the private military company Blackwater in 1997 (sold 2010), chaired the Hong Kong-listed Frontier Services Group backed by China's state CITIC Group until 2021, and now runs Vectus Global. A UN panel found in 2021 he broke the Libya arms embargo; in 2025–26 his men worked with the governments of Ecuador, Haiti and the DR Congo.
orgs.cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya 2021; Reuters 2025–26
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows open security contracts with governments and a breach of the Libya arms embargo, which are mercenary contracting and sanctions-breaking, not infiltration.

orgs.n: Russian state energy companies (Rosneft, Gazprom, Nord Stream)
orgs.d: Russia's state-controlled oil and gas companies and the Nord Stream pipeline company. They gave board seats to former European leaders, including German ex-chancellor Gerhard Schröder (Nord Stream from 2006, Rosneft from 2017) and Austrian ex-foreign minister Karin Kneissl (Rosneft 2021–22).
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows former European leaders taking board seats after leaving office, not anyone placed inside a government or international body while in post.

orgs.d: The largest Orthodox church, led since 2009 by Patriarch Kirill, who backs Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Its affiliated churches in neighbouring states have become targets of state action: Ukraine banned it by law in 2024, Estonia expelled the Moscow Patriarchate's metropolitan in 2024, and Latvia legislated its Orthodox church's independence in 2022. The UK, Canada and Ukraine sanctioned Kirill in 2022.
orgs.cite: Wikipedia 'Patriarch Kirill of Moscow' and articles on the Ukrainian, Estonian and Latvian churches
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a church backing a war and neighbouring states acting against its affiliates, not anyone placed inside those states' institutions.

orgs.d: A Saudi-funded international Islamic organisation founded in Mecca in 1962 to spread Islam abroad. A 1983 Belgian decree put the Great Mosque of Brussels under its control; Belgium ended the Saudi concession in 2018 on the recommendation of the parliamentary inquiry into the 2016 Brussels bombings. Its money also paid the first imams of Germany's DITIB.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a Saudi-funded body openly given control of a mosque and paying imams, not people placed inside a government, international body or company.

orgs.n: Gulf state and private Salafi missionary funding networks
orgs.d: A key for Salafi mosque and preacher funding that a government body has documented as coming from Gulf states or donors there, when no single named organisation is identified. The Dutch parliamentary inquiry of 2020 named donors from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar and listed amounts given to individual Dutch mosques.
orgs.cite: Dutch parliamentary inquiry, 25 Jun 2020, via DutchNews
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows Gulf donors funding mosques, which are not government bodies, international bodies or companies, with no one placed inside such institutions.

orgs.n: Diyanet (Presidency of Religious Affairs, Turkey) and its foreign branches (DITIB, ATIB)
orgs.d: Turkey's state religious directorate, founded in 1924. It writes the weekly sermon for about 85,000 mosques in Turkey and more than 2,000 abroad, employs imams as civil servants, and had a 2019 budget estimated at €1.7 billion. Its foreign arms include DITIB in Germany and ATIB in Austria. In 2016 it gave Turkey's parliament 50 reports from 38 countries on suspected Gülen followers gathered through its imams.
orgs.cite: Wikipedia 'Presidency of Religious Affairs'; Hürriyet Daily News 2016
orgs.reach_src: Case records (government actions or findings in each country)
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows open Turkish state control of mosques and imams abroad and imams reporting on individuals, not anyone placed inside a foreign government, international body or company.

orgs.d: A non-trinitarian church founded in Guadalajara in 1926 by Aarón Joaquín and led by his descendants. Its third leader, Naasón Joaquín García, was honoured at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in May 2019 at a senator's request, arrested in Los Angeles weeks later, and in June 2022 pleaded guilty to child sexual abuse and was sentenced to 16 years and 8 months. He continues to lead the church from prison.
orgs.cite: Wikipedia 'La Luz del Mundo' and 'Naasón Joaquín García'
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a church leader honoured at a senator's request and later convicted of child sexual abuse, not the church placing members inside government.

orgs.n: Lazarus Group / TraderTraitor (North Korean state hackers)
orgs.d: Hacking units of North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau that steal cryptocurrency and break into companies, often through suppliers and fake job offers. The FBI attributed the US$1.5 billion Bybit theft of February 2025 to them.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows hacking and theft of cryptocurrency, which breaks into computer systems but does not place people, money or control inside an institution.

orgs.d: Russia's foreign intelligence service. The US government attributed the 2019–20 SolarWinds Orion supply-chain intrusion to it in 2021.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a hacking operation through software updates, not people, money or control placed inside an institution.

orgs.d: Israel's foreign intelligence agency. According to the New York Times it ran BAC Consulting in Budapest and other shell firms that supplied booby-trapped pagers to Hezbollah under a Taiwanese brand licence; Israel's prime minister acknowledged the operation in November 2024.
orgs.cite: PM Netanyahu statement 10 Nov 2024; New York Times
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a front company Mossad set up itself to sell booby-trapped pagers to Hezbollah, not an existing government body, international body or company being penetrated.

orgs.d: Presidential decree of April 2023 letting the Russian state take over management of assets owned by companies from 'unfriendly' countries; used against Fortum, Uniper, Danone and Carlsberg in 2023.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows the Russian state openly seizing management of foreign-owned assets by decree, which is declared confiscation, not hidden infiltration.

orgs.d: Turkish state fund that became trustee of companies seized by the government; it took over 784 companies accused of Gülen links after 2015–16 and controlled 1,056 businesses in all by October 2025.
orgs.cite: Turkish Treasury figures via Anadolu Agency
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a Turkish state fund openly taking over seized companies, which is declared state confiscation, not hidden infiltration.

orgs.d: Private Shandong energy and logistics company owned by Ye Cheng, who has close ties to the Chinese Communist Party; holds a 99-year lease of Port Darwin (2015) that Australia now seeks to reverse.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows an openly signed port lease, not hidden placement of people or control.

orgs.d: China's state-owned power-grid company, the world's largest utility; owns 40% of the Philippines' national grid operator and holds grid stakes in several other countries.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows an open, declared shareholding in the Philippine grid operator, not hidden placement of people or control.

orgs.d: Chinese state-backed memory-chip maker charged in the US (2018) with Micron trade-secret theft through UMC engineers; put on the US export blacklist in 2018 and acquitted at trial in February 2024.
orgs.cite: US District Court N.D. California, 27 Feb 2024
orgs.drop_reason: Fujian Jinhua was acquitted at trial in February 2024, so the record does not establish that it placed or used insiders.

orgs.d: Jihadist armed movement that held territory in Syria and Iraq in 2014–19 and took payments from companies operating there, including Lafarge (convicted in Paris, April 2026).
orgs.cite: Paris Criminal Court 13 Apr 2026; US plea Oct 2022
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a company (Lafarge) paying an armed group to keep a factory running, which is extortion and terrorist financing, not ISIS placing people or control inside a government, international body or company.

orgs.d: Largest US oil company. In 2021 its federal lobbyist was filmed describing weekly contact with a key senator's office and use of 'shadow groups'.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows open lobbying and use of front groups described by a lobbyist, not ExxonMobil placing people, payments or control inside a government body.

orgs.d: US aluminium group whose French unit made the Reynobond PE cladding on Grenfell Tower. The inquiry found it obtained UK certification on a false basis.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: Obtaining certification on a false basis is fraud by the company's own staff, not an outside party getting inside a government body or company.

orgs.d: Insulation maker owned by France's Saint-Gobain. The Grenfell inquiry found it rigged a full-scale fire test of its RS5000 boards.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: Rigging a fire test is fraud by the company's own staff, not an outside party placing people or control inside an institution.

orgs.d: Irish building-materials group. The Grenfell inquiry found its tests of Kooltherm K15 insulation concealed components and that it misled the market about suitability for tall buildings.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: Concealing test components and misleading the market is fraud by the company itself, not infiltration of a government body or company.

orgs.d: US online retailer and cloud provider. The European Parliament withdrew its lobbyists' 14 access badges in February 2024 after it refused to attend hearings.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: Losing lobbyist access badges for refusing to attend hearings is a dispute over open lobbying, not Amazon getting people or control inside the European Parliament.

orgs.d: German payments company that collapsed in 2020 after €1.9 billion was found missing. The financial regulator BaFin had banned short-selling of its shares and pursued critics.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a regulator failing to supervise a fraudulent company and attacking its critics, not an outside party placing people or control inside BaFin or Wirecard.

orgs.d: French maker of the Rafale fighter. A French judge has investigated the 2016 sale of 36 Rafales to India since 2021.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows only an open French investigation into the 2016 Rafale sale, with no finding of anyone placed or paid inside India's government.

orgs.d: Trade association of pesticide and seed makers (Bayer, BASF, Syngenta, Corteva and others). Signed a letter of intent with the UN FAO in October 2020.
orgs.cite: FAO letter of intent, 2020; PAN International
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: A published letter of intent with the FAO is an open, declared agreement, and the record shows nothing hidden or anyone placed inside the FAO.

orgs.d: Brazilian iron ore miner whose Brumadinho dam collapsed in 2019 after German auditor TÜV SÜD certified it stable; both were charged in 2020.
orgs.reach_src: Cases in corp_cases.json and the cited forums.
orgs.drop_reason: A false safety certificate before the dam collapse is the subject of homicide and fraud charges, but the record shows no outside party placed or paid inside a government body.

orgs.d: Criminal group that grew out of Venezuela's Tocorón prison and spread with Venezuelan migration to Colombia, Peru, Chile and the United States. The US designated it a foreign terrorist organisation in 2025; US intelligence agencies assessed that the Maduro government does not direct it.
orgs.cite: US National Intelligence Council memo, April 2025
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a gang spreading abroad and being designated a terrorist organisation, and US intelligence found the Venezuelan government does not direct it, so no one is shown inside an institution.

orgs.d: Network around convicted crime boss Alaattin Çakıcı, a former Grey Wolves member once used by Turkish intelligence for operations abroad. He was freed under a 2020 sentence-reduction law after the MHP leader called for his amnesty.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a state using a criminal abroad and a party leader lobbying for his release, not the network placing people or control inside Turkish institutions.

orgs.d: St Petersburg crime groups of the 1990s. Spain's Operation Troika (2008) accused their leaders, including Gennady Petrov, of laundering money in Spain; in 2018 Spain's National Court acquitted the 17 Russians tried, including a Duma deputy.
orgs.drop_reason: The record ends in a 2018 acquittal of all 17 Russians tried, so it does not establish anyone placed inside a government or company.

orgs.d: Banned Kenyan sect and gang that ran extortion in Nairobi's minibus transport and slums. The Waki Commission linked it to organised revenge attacks in the 2007–08 post-election violence; ICC charges against Uhuru Kenyatta over it were withdrawn in 2014.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a gang used for extortion and political violence, with charges against a politician withdrawn, not the gang placing people inside a government body or company.

orgs.d: Formed by the 1955 merger of the Rockefeller-linked Chase National Bank and the Bank of the Manhattan Company; David Rockefeller was its president from 1960 and chairman and chief executive from 1969 to 1980/81, also chairing the Council on Foreign Relations (1970–85) and founding the Trilateral Commission (1973). Chase opened the first US bank branch in Moscow (1973) and in 1979 led the campaign to admit the Shah of Iran to the US. It merged with J.P. Morgan & Co. in 2000.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows David Rockefeller openly lobbying President Carter and chairing policy bodies, not placing, paying or secretly controlling anyone inside government.

orgs.d: Founded in 1930 under the Young Plan to handle German reparations, owned by member central banks, and the oldest international financial institution. It hosts closed meetings of central bank governors (monthly in the 1930s, every two months since 1998) and the Basel Committee whose capital rules countries adopt. In 1939 it transferred Czechoslovakia's gold to the Reichsbank; the 1944 Bretton Woods conference called for its liquidation, reversed in 1948. Carroll Quigley called it 'the apex' of a private world system of financial control.
orgs.cite: Wikipedia 'Bank for International Settlements'; Quigley, Tragedy and Hope pp. 324–325
orgs.drop_reason: The BIS is an open body owned by central banks; its gold transfer and closed meetings are its own conduct, and Quigley's 'apex of control' is an opinion, not a record of anyone placed inside institutions.

orgs.d: St Petersburg bank whose largest shareholder is Yury Kovalchuk; the US Treasury called it 'the personal bank for senior officials of the Russian Federation' when sanctioning it in March 2014. It expanded into annexed Crimea and is under US, EU and other sanctions.
orgs.drop_reason: The record shows a bank owned by Putin's associates and sanctioned by the US, but not that it placed, paid or controlled anyone inside an institution.

orgs.d: Ukraine's largest bank, co-founded by Ihor Kolomoisky and Gennadiy Bogolyubov; nationalised in December 2016 with a $5.6 billion bailout after insider lending. Kolomoisky was designated by the US for significant corruption in 2021 and arrested in Ukraine in 2023. The bank is now state-owned.
orgs.drop_reason: PrivatBank's losses came from insider lending by its own owners and managers, with no outside party getting inside an institution.

orgs.d: Philanthropy founded in 1913 from the Standard Oil fortune of John D. Rockefeller; by the 1920s the world's largest. Its International Health Division ran campaigns with governments, it funded League of Nations bodies and the Institute of Pacific Relations, and its 1943 Mexican Agriculture Program began the Green Revolution later spread to India and elsewhere.
orgs.drop_reason: The Rockefeller Foundation's grants to the League of Nations and its farming programmes were open, declared funding, not hidden placement or control.

orgs.d: The NSA is the US signals-intelligence agency. Documents leaked by Edward Snowden in 2013 showed it monitoring allied leaders, EU institutions and UN headquarters, often with partner services such as Denmark's FE and Germany's BND.
orgs.drop_reason: The record is eavesdropping and hacking by a spy agency; it shows no people, money or control placed inside the bodies spied on to steer their decisions.

orgs.d: GCHQ is the UK's signals-intelligence agency. Snowden documents showed it intercepting delegates at the 2009 London G20 and hacking Belgium's state telecom Belgacom in 2010–2013.
orgs.drop_reason: Intercepting G20 delegates and hacking Belgacom are spying and hacking, with no people, money or control placed inside to steer decisions.

orgs.d: Australia's foreign intelligence service. In 2004 it bugged Timor-Leste's cabinet room during Timor Sea oil-and-gas talks; the resulting treaty was later replaced.
orgs.drop_reason: Bugging Timor-Leste's cabinet room is espionage; no people, money or control were placed inside Timor-Leste's government.

orgs.d: Tel Aviv political marketing firm that, per the New York Times, ran a roughly $2m covert social-media campaign aimed at US lawmakers for Israel's Ministry of Diaspora Affairs in 2023–24. Meta banned it in May 2024.
orgs.cite: New York Times, June 2024; Meta threat report May 2024
orgs.drop_reason: STOIC ran fake social-media accounts aimed at US lawmakers from outside; nobody was placed, paid or controlled inside Congress.

orgs.d: Geneva private intelligence firm founded by Mario Brero. Leaked files reported in 2023 ('Abu Dhabi Secrets') show the UAE paid it at least €5.7m from 2017 to target about 1,000 people and 400 organisations in 18 European countries.
orgs.drop_reason: Alp Services ran a smear and intelligence campaign against people and groups for the UAE; the record shows no one placed or paid inside a government, international body or company.

orgs.d: Emirati cyber firm that from 2016 ran Project Raven, a UAE surveillance unit staffed partly by former US intelligence operatives, which Reuters reported targeted Qatar's emir, activists and journalists. Three ex-US operatives signed US deferred-prosecution agreements in 2021.
orgs.drop_reason: Project Raven was the UAE's own hacking unit staffed by hired former US operatives; it spied on targets from outside rather than placing anyone inside their institutions.

orgs.n: GRU (Main Directorate of the General Staff), Russia
orgs.d: Russia's military intelligence service. Its officers were caught trying to hack the OPCW in The Hague in 2018 and were indicted in the US for hacking WADA after the McLaren report.
orgs.cite: Dutch MoD Oct 2018; US indictment Oct 2018
orgs.drop_reason: The GRU's attempts to hack the OPCW and WADA are cyber-attacks from outside; nobody was placed, paid or controlled inside those bodies.

orgs.n: Office of the High Representative (OHR), Bosnia and Herzegovina
orgs.d: International office created by the 1995 Dayton agreement and overseen by the Peace Implementation Council of foreign governments. Its 1997 'Bonn powers' let it impose laws and dismiss Bosnian officials (139 removed by 2004).
orgs.drop_reason: The High Representative's powers in Bosnia are open and set by the Dayton agreement; nothing is hidden or beyond what was agreed.

orgs.d: Regional central bank issuing the Central African CFA franc for six states. Under its arrangement with France, the French Treasury guarantees the peg and members deposit half their reserves with it.
orgs.drop_reason: France's guarantee and the reserve-deposit rule are open treaty terms of the CFA franc, not hidden placement or control.

orgs.n: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW)
orgs.d: Treaty body that enforces the Chemical Weapons Convention. In April 2018 four GRU officers were caught trying to hack its Wi-Fi network while it investigated the Salisbury Novichok poisoning.
orgs.drop_reason: The GRU's attempt to hack the OPCW's Wi-Fi was stopped from outside the building; nobody got inside the organisation.

orgs.d: Russian property and energy group of Russian-Armenian billionaire Samvel Karapetyan; ran Electric Networks of Armenia until Armenia moved to nationalise it after his 2025 arrest.
orgs.drop_reason: Tashir Group ran Armenia's power grid under an open concession, and its owner's arrest was over political statements; nothing shows it placing or paying people inside the state.

orgs.d: Chinese Communist Party department that handles relations with foreign political parties. In Dec 2020 its vice-minister Guo Yezhou led a delegation to Nepal during the split in the ruling Nepal Communist Party.
orgs.drop_reason: A Chinese party delegation openly urging unity in Nepal's ruling party is diplomacy, with no one placed or paid inside Nepal's institutions.

orgs.n: Wan Kuok-koi and World Hongmen History and Culture Association
orgs.d: Association led by former 14K triad boss Wan Kuok-koi, sanctioned by the US in 2020 as a criminal front; OCCRP documented its 2018–2019 attempt to set up a casino zone in Palau with former Palauan officials as directors.
orgs.drop_reason: Wan Kuok-koi's Palau association used former officials as directors and its casino plan was rejected; no one inside Palau's government was placed or paid.

orgs.d: Swiss bank. A Papua New Guinea Commission of Inquiry (2021) found the 2014 UBS-arranged loan to buy Oil Search shares unlawful and recommended a 10-year ban on UBS in PNG.
orgs.cite: PNG Commission of Inquiry into the UBS Loan
orgs.drop_reason: The PNG inquiry found the government's own loan unlawful; UBS earned fees but the record shows no one placed or paid inside the government.

orgs.d: Andorran bank named a primary money-laundering concern by FinCEN in 2015 and taken over by the state; FinCEN withdrew the finding in 2016 and Spanish courts later cleared it.
orgs.drop_reason: FinCEN withdrew its finding and Spanish courts cleared the bank, so the record does not show a crime group inside it.

orgs.d: Closed German religious sect (Sociedad Benefactora y Educacional Dignidad) that collaborated with Pinochet's DINA; none of the listed keys fits

orgs.drop_reason: Colonia Dignidad was a sect whose compound Pinochet's secret police used for torture; the state used the sect rather than the sect getting inside the state.

orgs.d: Organisation armée secrète: clandestine organisation formed in 1961 by French army officers to block Algerian independence.
orgs.reach_src: countries where this map holds a documented case
orgs.drop_reason: The OAS was a revolt by French army officers themselves; the record shows a putsch and terrorism, not an outside party placing people inside institutions.

orgs.d: Asekätkentä (Weapons Cache Case): secret network organised from Finnish Military Headquarters after the 1944 armistice to hide weapons for a guerrilla force.
orgs.reach_src: countries where this map holds a documented case
orgs.drop_reason: The Weapons Cache network was organised by Finland's own military headquarters, with no outside party getting inside the state.

channels.n: Condor founding: Santiago → Buenos Aires → Montevideo → Asunción → La Paz
channels.d: Chile's DINA convened intelligence chiefs in Santiago on 25 November 1975; Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia signed the founding document in January 1976. Members shared intelligence and carried out cross-border kidnappings, torture and killings; Automotores Orletti in Buenos Aires was a key detention site.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor expansion: Santiago → Brasília → Lima → Quito
channels.d: Brazil became a formal member in 1976; Peru and Ecuador joined in 1977–78. In 1980 Peruvian and Argentine agents kidnapped four Montonero militants in Lima, one of the last recorded Condor operations.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor phase three: Santiago → Washington (Letelier, 1976)
channels.d: Former Chilean ambassador Orlando Letelier and Ronni Moffitt were killed by a car bomb in Washington in September 1976; an FBI report suggested it may have been a Condor 'phase three' mission. The Letelier case led to the 1979 public revelation of Condor.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor: La Paz exile killed in Buenos Aires (1976)
channels.d: Former Bolivian president Juan José Torres was assassinated in Buenos Aires in 1976, a case listed among Condor's cross-border killings.

channels.n: Safari Club: Riyadh money, Paris airlift, Rabat & Cairo troops → Shaba (Zaire, 1977)
channels.d: Saudi Arabia paid, France supplied technology and Egypt and Morocco provided troops. In 1977 French aircraft flew Moroccan and Egyptian troops into Zaire's Shaba province to repel an invasion.

channels.n: Safari Club arms: Cairo → Mogadishu (Ogaden war)
channels.d: The club supplied arms to Somalia in exchange for Siad Barre distancing himself from the Soviet Union during the Ogaden war. BCCI reportedly helped finance and launder money for the club's operations.

channels.n: Aginter Press: Lisbon → Milan / Rome (explosives training)
channels.d: Judge Guido Salvini found Aginter instructors trained members of the Italian neo-fascist Avanguardia Nazionale in explosives, and linked the agency to the groups behind the December 1969 Piazza Fontana bombing in Milan.

channels.n: Aginter Press: Lisbon → Luanda / Lourenço Marques (colonial wars)
channels.d: Aginter allegedly worked against independence movements in Portugal's colonies of Angola, Mozambique and East Timor; disputed sources tie it to the killings of Amílcar Cabral and Eduardo Mondlane.

channels.n: Aginter Press flight: Lisbon → Alicante / Caracas (1974)
channels.d: After the April 1974 Carnation Revolution, members fled to a site near Alicante associated with the Paladin Group, and the agency reportedly escaped to Caracas.

channels.n: TFP spread: São Paulo → Buenos Aires / Santiago / Montevideo (1967) → Warsaw
channels.d: From the Brazilian TFP (1960), national TFPs were founded in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay in 1967 and in Poland in 1995; Poland's Ordo Iuris was founded in 2013 by the TFP-linked Christian Culture Association.

channels.n: NXIVM: Albany → Mexico City / Vancouver
channels.d: NXIVM ran centres in Mexico and Canada as well as the US; Emiliano Salinas, son of former president Carlos Salinas, and Ana Cristina Fox, daughter of Vicente Fox, have been accused of involvement, and the Vancouver chapter recruited actresses including Allison Mack.

channels.n: Kingdom of Jesus Christ: Davao → California / Hawaii
channels.d: A US grand jury indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for child sex trafficking and misuse of church donations; FBI raids hit church sites in California, Texas and Hawaii.

channels.n: Saudi trust account through the US Treasury
channels.d: Saudi money deposited in a US Treasury trust account paid for US technical staff placed in Saudi agencies under the 1974 Joint Commission.

channels.n: NED grants to Venezuela's Cedice
channels.d: From 1998 NED's business institute CIPE made regular grants to Cedice, Atlas's Caracas think tank, whose director signed the 2002 Carmona Decree.

channels.n: Pilgrims Society: London ↔ New York, 1902–03
channels.d: The London society (1902) and New York society (1903) hold reciprocal membership and welcome each other's ambassadors.

channels.n: Fuzhou and Qingtian police bureaus to European 'service stations'
channels.d: Safeguard Defenders listed stations run for the Fuzhou city police in Dublin, Prato, Budapest, Paris, Prague and Athens, among others.

channels.n: Qingtian county police to stations in Rome, Milan, Florence, Vienna, Frankfurt
channels.d: Stations listed for the Qingtian County Public Security Bureau, a home county of many Chinese migrants in Italy and Austria.

channels.n: Moscow to Paris — Front National bank loan
channels.d: €9 million loan from the First Czech Russian Bank to the Front National, 2014.

channels.n: Ankara Diyanet to DITIB Cologne
channels.d: DITIB's imams are trained in Ankara and paid as Turkish civil servants by the Diyanet.

channels.n: Erik Prince's security deals with governments, 2019–2026
channels.d: A UN panel found Prince broke the Libya arms embargo in 2019; in 2025–26 he made security deals with Ecuador's president, ran anti-gang operations in Haiti through Vectus Global, and sent men and drones to help Congo's army at Uvira.
channels.cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, Feb 2021; Reuters 2025–26

channels.n: Diyanet imam network in Western Europe
channels.d: Turkey's Diyanet sends state-employed imams to mosques run by its branches abroad. Germany investigated DITIB imams for spying (2017), Austria reviewed the permits of about 40 ATIB imams (2018), a Dutch parliamentary inquiry found strong Diyanet political influence (2020), and Belgian State Security found a Diyanet employee in the new Brussels mosque body (2020).
channels.cite: Politico Europe 2017; Al Jazeera 2018; DutchNews 2020; Belgian Justice Ministry 2020

channels.n: Gulf Salafi funding to Belgian and Dutch mosques
channels.d: The Muslim World League ran the Great Mosque of Brussels for Saudi Arabia until Belgium ended the lease in 2018; the 2020 Dutch parliamentary inquiry traced Salafi mosque funding to donors in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar.

channels.n: Moscow Patriarchate churches cut off by neighbouring states
channels.d: After the 2022 invasion, Latvia (2022), Estonia (2024) and Ukraine (2024) used laws, residence permits and bans to sever local Orthodox churches from the Moscow Patriarchate.
channels.cite: Wikipedia articles on the Latvian, Estonian and Ukrainian churches; ERR News

channels.n: Basel: central bank governors' meetings
channels.d: Governors of the main central banks have met privately in Basel since 1930, monthly in the 1930s and every two months since 1998; Quigley described this as the apex of a world system of financial control.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Bank for International Settlements'; Quigley, Tragedy and Hope p. 324

channels.n: NSA access to Danish cables used to spy on European leaders (2012–14)
channels.d: Per the Danish FE's 'Dunhammer' review, the NSA used Danish cable intercepts to wiretap German leaders, with reported targets in Sweden, Norway and France.

channels.n: UAE money to Alp Services to target Europeans (2017–21)
channels.d: At least €5.7m paid via an Emirati front to Alp, which compiled files on people in 18 European countries, with the largest counts in Belgium, Italy and Norway.
